role: The shared living-entity header: the kind enum for every mob, damage source families, attribute records, the AI task, navigator, look/move/jump/body helper and senses records, the struct living that carries every kind's state, the entity list and per-chunk section structs (an_world), and the prototypes of living.c plus the per-kind files (hostiles*.c, villagers.c, animals.c, ai.c, blaze).

structs.name: attr_mod
structs.java: AttributeModifier: amount, operation, name, id (UUID), isSaved, plus a held-item flag

structs.name: attr_instance
structs.java: ModifiableAttributeInstance: baseValue, cachedValue, needsUpdate, the modifiers (fixed 8)

structs.name: ai_task
structs.java: the union of every EntityAIBase subclass's fields, selected by cls

structs.name: equip_slot
structs.java: an equipment ItemStack: id, damage, count and its tag (itemtag.h)

structs.name: living
structs.java: Entity, EntityLivingBase, EntityLiving, EntityCreature, EntityAgeable, EntityAnimal and every kind subclass's fields (villager, golem, slime, player food, squid, bat, chicken, zombie, pigman, skeleton, witch, blaze, ghast, creeper, enderman, spider) in one record

structs.name: an_ent
structs.java: one World.loadedEntityList entry (living or item-world entity)

structs.name: an_chunk
structs.java: Chunk.entityLists: 16 y sections of entity pointers (fixed 2048 each)

structs.name: an_world
structs.java: World.loadedEntityList plus the chunk sections, skylightSubtracted, the player list stand-in and the replay hooks

gpu: struct living: a 4,216-byte hot record (was 23,440; 6,512 before lane/entmem named attribute modifiers by id) with every kind's fields; the AI task lists and door list (living_ai), the villager's trades (living_villager) and the probe player's inventory (living_player) are pools of their own, a slot taken when first reached (ai_part, villager_part, player_part); senses are one per env (env.h senses); references to other livings are lrefs; l->world, l->an and player_sp stay addresses of containers (lane/gpuarena, L3; lane/entmem)

struct ai_task: 120 bytes, the shared fields then each class's own in an anonymous union (lane/entmem); target, mate, golem and child are lrefs, the front door a door-pool slot + 1, the village an index + 1 in its collection, the paths pathrefs (lane/gpuarena, L3)
line 191-194, struct path_nav: pointers to a path, the path finder and a heap int buffer
struct an_world: the list holds an_ent pool slots; the chunk table comes from the arena slab (lane/gpuarena, L3)
struct an_chunk: 16 sec_list slot-index lists in the arena slab (lane/gpuarena, L3)
lines 536-561, struct an_world: several replay and probe callbacks as function pointers
line 544, struct an_world: jrand *shuf_rand pointer to an external Random
notes: Several prototypes are declared twice (living_init, living_set_size, living_is_movement_blocked, living_dmg_unblockable), harmless. The kind enum values double as class selectors for queries (living_kind_in_class). Fixed capacities: AI_MAX_ENTRIES 24, ATTR_MAX_MODS 8, AN_MAX_ENTITIES 4096 (an_list_push stops loudly past it). Java field names in the struct mirrors were matched by grep against the Java files, not by reading every access.
